Ash weight isn't a good measure so much as volume.

  • A cremated body produces approximately 1 cubic inch of ash per pound of body weight (mortuary rule of thumb).

  • Assuming an average of 100lbs per body, you have 600m pounds of corpse, resulting in 600m cubic inches of ash.

  • 3√(600,000,000) = roughly 843 inches on a side. 843/12 = 70.25 feet on each side, call it 70 for argument's sake.

  • 70x70x70 cube with Auschwitz for scale

That volume is handled easily enough by a small fleet of trucks and can be moved/dispersed elsewhere with relative ease.

The argument that needs to be driven home is the astronomical fuel burn involved in cremating millions of bodies. The 2-3 hour figure comes from modern mortuary guidelines, which is why people use it. If they were burning bodies in 25 minutes, they would be using far more fuel than a normal cremation, because they would have to get absolutely ridiculous levels of heat. And with increased heat comes increased maintenance requirements.

If they were burning multiple bodies at once, that increases the thermal mass, thus requiring even more fuel on top of the already obscene amounts they'd have to be burning.
